concepts.def: Random Access Memory: volatile main memory holding running programs and data.
Read Only Memory: non-volatile memory holding firmware such as the bootloader.
Uses part of secondary storage as if it were RAM when main memory is full.
Hard Disk Drive: magnetic spinning-platter storage with high capacity but slower access than SSD.
Solid State Drive: flash-memory storage with no moving parts, faster than HDD.
Storage on CD, DVD or Blu-ray, read by a laser; useful for long-term distribution.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Memory & Storage — a core area of GCSE Computer Science.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Memory & Storage brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Memory & Storage.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: What does it mean that RAM is volatile?
options: It can store data permanently.
It can explode or be damaged easily.
Its contents are lost when power is removed.

mcqs.q: What happens when 11111111 + 1 is computed in an 8-bit register?
options: The computer crashes.
It just becomes 100000000 normally.
Overflow - the result requires 9 bits but only 8 are available.

mcqs.q: How many layers are in the OSI model?
options: The computer crashes.
7 (Physical, Data Link, Network, Transport, Session, Presentation, Application).
4 (confusing with TCP/IP model).
